prompt: Review this code. A NestJS service enqueues transactional emails onto a BullMQ queue and, to make enqueuing idempotent, builds a deterministic job id from the logical unit of work (`welcome:${userId}`) so BullMQ refuses a second job with the same id while one is still present. Walk me through whether this actually guarantees "send at most once," and call out anything you'd block on before this ships. If you find a problem, tell me how you'd fix it and how you'd test that the fix holds.
